conflicts.fact: Bacterial doubling arithmetic / cell number growth over time
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says a bacterium dividing every 20 minutes gives 64 cells after 2 hours (6 divisions, which is correct: 2^6=64). Lesson 7 asks 'If one cell divides every 24 hours, how many cells after 10 days?' with answer 1024 (2^10, correct). No actual conflict in arithmetic, so only a minor concern.

conflicts.fact: Stages of mitosis taught: whether interphase is part of the stage sequence
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says mitosis has four stages (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase) followed by cytokinesis. Lesson 7 lists five stages, with interphase as stage 1 and telophase+cytokinesis as stage 5, and calls the drawings a 'cycle'.

conflicts.fact: Meiosis/mitosis cell counts and timing of the 'asexual reproduction' question and lesson numbering
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 teacher notes say the questions flag Lesson 9 (budding and binary fission), but budding and binary fission is Lesson 6, and Lesson 9 is consolidation/animations.

conflicts.fact: Group size for the same activities
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10 use groups of 5-6; Lesson 4 uses groups of 6 to 8; Lesson 9 uses groups of 6-8 (home groups of 4 in the jigsaw); Lesson 8 uses 4-6.

conflicts.fact: Mitosis vs meiosis role statements: Lesson 4 DQB question vs Lesson 8 statement 'Meiosis is more important than mitosis for growth'; and Lesson 5 says meiosis gives variation while Lesson 8 flags DQB item on binary fission and mitosis
conflicts.versions: No incompatible fact; only a distractor statement.

conflicts.fact: Plant/organism used and root growth data
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says the onion root 'grew 3 cm in five days' and elsewhere says it was grown for a week and 'lengthened by several centimetres'; Lesson 3 uses an onion root tip diagram with 4 chromosomes whereas Lesson 2 says maize has 20 chromosomes (no conflict).
